question: Al Jazeera reported on Tuesday, 9 January 2024 about protests in Pakistan against enforced disappearances of people living in Balochistan province1. The immediate cause is the disappearance and death of Balaach Mola Baksh. According to a Pakistani commission of enquiry, more than 2 700 people have disappeared since 2011 after being abducted by the security forces. Many of them have been found dead years later. 1.

Is the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy aware of what is termed the ‘kill and dump’ policy of the Pakistani security services and, if so, what does he think about it?
What is the EU doing as part of its policy towards Pakistan to put an end to these practices and assist victims?
In its bilateral relationship with Pakistan, how will the EU work to improve human rights in that country, and is this a reason for the EU to review Pakistan's GSP+ status?
answer: The EU is well aware of the problem of enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings in Pakistan. The EU engages with Pakistan on the implementation of international commitments in the area of human rights, amongst others on the seven human rights conventions, upon which the granted status of trade facilitation ‘Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus’ (GSP+) is conditional.

During bilateral dialogues and in United Nations’ human rights fora, as well as through diplomatic channels, the EU addresses various shortcomings in the area of human rights. The most recent GSP implementation report published on 21 November 2023 includes a Staff Working Document on Pakistan. In that report, enforced disappearances are highlighted as an important remaining concern.

As the report states, additional legislation in this field would align Pakistan’s legal framework with its international commitments. A Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill 2021, which aims to amend the Pakistani penal code to include enforced disappearances, was discussed by both chambers of the Parliament but has not been adopted. The EU will continuously monitor the situation.
